column2: Number of spikes assigned to the cluster after curation edits (count); 0 for an empty cluster.
Mean firing rate in Hz over the whole recording, n_spikes divided by n_samples / sample_rate; 0 when the recording has zero duration.
Mean per-spike amplitude in the sorter's amplitude units (raw ADC counts for int16 data, µV only when the input is calibrated); NaN when the cluster has no amplitudes.
Fraction (0-1) of 50 equal-duration bins across the recording that contain at least one spike; 0 for an empty cluster.
Count of consecutive inter-spike intervals shorter than the configured fixed refractory window (default 1.5 ms).
ISI violations per second of the cluster's own first-to-last spike span (a rate, not a fraction); 0 with fewer than 2 spikes.
Estimated fraction (0-0.5) of spikes missed below the detection threshold, from a 30-bin mirror-tail fit of the amplitude histogram; 0 with fewer than 8 spikes.
Absolute mean divided by the sample SD of per-spike amplitudes (dimensionless); 0 with fewer than 2 spikes or zero SD.
Pearson correlation (-1 to 1) between spike time and per-spike amplitude; 0 with fewer than 3 spikes or constant values.
Longest silent stretch, including before the first and after the last spike, as a fraction (0-1) of the recording duration; 1.0 for an empty cluster.
Geometric mean (0-1) of the contamination, presence, coverage, SNR, completeness and stability sub-scores, plus the isolation score when available.
Squared Mahalanobis distance to the n_in-th nearest background spike in a 3-PC subspace of template-relative channel 0; NaN under 50 cluster spikes, no PC features, or too few background spikes.

Mean chi-squared survival (df = 3 PCs) of background spikes' Mahalanobis squared distances divided by n_in; lower is better; NaN under 50 cluster spikes, no PC features, or ill-conditioned covariance.
Fraction (0-1) of the 8 nearest neighbours, in a background-balanced PC pool, that belong to the cluster; NaN with fewer than 2 cluster spikes or no background.
Standardized separation of cluster and background means along the Fisher LDA axis in PC space (dimensionless, about 4 or more is well isolated); NaN if either class has fewer than 2 spikes.
Mean of (b - a) / max(a, b) over cluster spikes, with a and b the distances to the cluster and background centroids in PC space; range -1 to 1; NaN without both classes.
Milliseconds from the trough (minimum) to the following peak (maximum) of the primary template on its peak channel; NaN without seeded templates.
Width of the primary template's trough at half its depth, linearly interpolated, in milliseconds, on its peak channel; NaN without seeded templates.
Peak value after the trough divided by the absolute trough depth, for the primary template on its peak channel (dimensionless); NaN without seeded templates.
(peak - trough) / trough_to_peak_ms for the primary template on its peak channel, in amplitude units per millisecond; 0 when the trace never recovers; NaN without templates.
Count of interior local extrema in the primary template's peak-channel trace with magnitude at least 20% of the peak-to-peak amplitude; 3 or more suggests a multi-peak waveform.
X coordinate (µm) of the template footprint centroid, weighted by per-channel peak-to-peak amplitude squared; NaN without probe geometry or seeded templates.
Y coordinate (µm) of the template footprint centroid, weighted by per-channel peak-to-peak amplitude squared; NaN without probe geometry or seeded templates.
Decay length (µm) from a log-linear fit of per-channel peak-to-peak amplitude versus distance from the peak channel, over channels at 5%+ of the max; NaN without 3 such channels and a negative slope.
Radius (µm) around the footprint centroid that encloses 80% of the summed squared per-channel peak-to-peak amplitudes; NaN without seeded templates or probe geometry.
Count of channels whose peak-to-peak template amplitude is at least 20% of the maximum channel's; NaN without seeded templates or probe geometry.
Least-squares slope of per-channel trough time in ms versus distance from the peak channel over active channels, in ms per 100 µm; NaN with fewer than 3 active channels.
Mean autocorrelogram count at 2-10 ms lags divided by the mean at 30-50 ms lags, from a 1 ms-bin, +/-50 ms ACG (dimensionless); NaN when the baseline is 0 or the ACG is too short.

Refractory window in milliseconds with the lowest Hill contamination estimate on the configured grid (default: 0.75-10 ms in 0.25 ms steps), ties resolving to the longest window; NaN when no window could be estimated.
Hill false-positive fraction (0-1) at rp_estimate_ms, the estimated share of spikes that belong to other units; NaN when no refractory window could be estimated.
Hartigan dip statistic (0-0.25) of up to 5000 evenly strided per-spike amplitudes; larger values indicate a second amplitude mode; NaN with fewer than 4 amplitudes.
Least-squares slope of per-spike amplitude versus time in seconds, in amplitude units per second; NaN with fewer than 2 spikes or when spike and amplitude counts differ.

Nominal upper limit on the contamination fraction (0-1): the smallest that the sliding-RP test confirms at confidence above 90%, assuming diffuse (Poisson) contamination; NaN if none of the 0.5%-35% grid passes, which means either contamination above 35% or too few spikes to tell.
Tested refractory window (ms) of highest confidence at srp_contamination, the sliding-RP estimate of the refractory period; NaN when no tested combination passes.
Mean contamination fraction (0-1) at the fixed refractory window under a diffuse-contamination Poisson likelihood and uniform Beta(1,1) prior; conditional on that model.
Lower endpoint of the fixed-window contamination posterior's shortest 95% credible interval (fraction, 0-1).
Upper endpoint of the fixed-window contamination posterior's shortest 95% credible interval (fraction, 0-1).
Number of stable firing-rate and amplitude epochs inferred over the recording; NaN when not computed.
Smallest divided by largest magnitude of the epoch mean amplitudes; NaN if amplitudes were not fitted, any epoch is silent, or the largest magnitude is zero.
Lowest divided by highest epoch firing rate; 1 for one epoch, NaN when not computed.
Count of spikes that deduplication would discard at the default 0.2 ms tolerance.
